description:
FOUND + FIXED s526w2 (Opus, 2026-10-24), Pod-Simple-3.47 board census.  PRE-EXISTING on main b89b6add.  SILENT (the statement's real argument vanished; the failure surfaced later).

    use File::Spec; require File::Spec->catfile($dir, "ao.pl");   # ao.pl: sub ascii_order { $a cmp $b } 1;
    print join("|", sort ascii_order qw(b a c)), "\n";
  perl: a|b|c     PCL (main): dies "Undefined sort subroutine "main::ascii_order" called"; emission was (p-require "File::Spec")

CAUSE: Pl/Parser.pm _process_include_statement takes PPI's Statement::Include->module (the first bareword) as the module name; perl reads a bareword followed by `->` as a CLASS name in a method-call expression.  Not a PPI bug (the token stream is right; ->module is a convenience accessor).
FIX: when the module word's next significant sibling is `->`, $module = '' so the existing EXPRESSION path lowers the whole argument: (p-require-file (p-method-call (p-resolve-invocant "File::Spec") "catfile" ...)).  Probes (scratch/s526w2/preq.pl) perl = tree for: plain require, require-with-modifier, the method form, %INC, a missing file dying in eval.  Guard Pl/t/misc-fixes-01.t row 139, inverse-verified on a main extraction.
NOT covered: the EXPRESSION-context spelling (`my $v = require Foo->bar(...)`, Pl/ExprToCL.pm ~2671) -- not probed.
ROWS: Pod-Simple search10/12/20/22/26/28.t (*PLAN* rows; counted in the census).
subject: `require Class->method(...)` was lowered as `require Class` and the method call DROPPED without a word -- perl requires the file the call returns (Pod-Simple t/search*.t: `require File::Spec->catfile($t_dir, 'ascii_order.pl')`, then `sort ascii_order ...` died "Undefined sort subroutine")
